real_defects.issue: parseFees fee pattern [\d,]+ accepted a bare ',' as a $0 fee and '1,,0' as $10 with no error, so a typo in the editable fee table silently zeroed or shrank a bracket. Reproduced with node; fixed to digits with commas only as thousands separators, failing-first test added.

parseBenchmarks used [\d,]+ for band edges, so '$,-$,: 1' parsed as a 0-0 band and '1,,000' as 1000 with no error, and the percent [\d.]+ took '1.2.3' as NaN. Fixed to strict numbers; failing-first test.
plan() used num(grossReturn) || 6, so a typed 0% gross return silently projected at 6%. Fixed: blank or unreadable means 6, a typed 0 is used; failing-first test.

List fields read numbers with [\d.,]+ then stripped commas, so '$, at ,' was a $0 credit from 0 kWh up and '1.2.3 under ,' a NaN fee; energy tiers split on every comma, so '8.2 to 1,000' became a 1 kWh tier plus a 0 cent tier. Fixed: strict number check with a readable error, and commas between thousands groups no longer split tiers; failing-first test.
parseUsage month and bare lines captured kWh with [\d,]+, so '1,,0' was a 10 kWh month and a ',' line a 0 kWh month. Fixed to strict numbers; failing-first test.
